preconditions: One explicitly supplied immutable XML byte document and native per-document hard limits; no project writer or external resolver.
Owned JUnit XML and explicit versioned JSON mapping bytes plus supplied native VerificationTest/VerificationContract targets; no implicit inventory, external identifier, producer or run lookup.
Explicit immutable JUnit document, closed mapping rules, native supplied Test/Verification targets and, when selected, a sidecar bound to the exact XML SHA-256 and core occurrence ordinals.
steps: Read complete suites and testcases with the documented children and attributes, retaining original bytes/hash and reported strings without evaluating outcomes.
Reject DTD/entity declarations, external schema/include requests, processing instructions, malformed XML and violated limits without file/network/process access.
Check exact boundary acceptance, immutable result ownership, opaque extensions and matching isolated Core/PYZ behavior.
Reject recursive, quadratic and exponential entity declarations before interpreting the DTD subset; reject schema/include references and processing instructions even inside opaque extensions.
Enforce combined namespace-declaration/attribute limits and cumulative expanded-name budgets at exact boundaries; retain literal CDATA and comment content without false positives.
Reject nonprofile declared encodings before extensible host codec lookup; prove all supported declarations and matching isolated Core/PYZ error contracts with file/network/process traps.
Resolve configured nonempty combinations of classname/name/file by exact decoded values to actual supplied target IDs, preserving testcase order and target revision/raw/canonical hashes.
Classify no core outcome marker as passed, failure/error as failed and skipped as skipped; retain separate occurrences and ignore suite totals and passive output strings.
Refuse the initial resolution completely for missing/unmapped/repeated keys, mixed outcome kinds, invalid mappings or absent/duplicate/untyped targets without publishing partial Evidence.

Verify original XML and mapping provenance, owned immutable results, isolated Core/PYZ parity, explicit composition with existing Evidence construction and absence of file/network/process/clock/entropy access.

Resolve configurable combinations of classname/name/file/external_id; keep same names with different selected Class/File contexts distinct, never infer an identifier from unknown XML or target metadata.

Account for every testcase occurrence and return separate unmapped, ambiguous and contradictory diagnostics with grouped occurrence/mapping indices; retain only independently unambiguous candidates without choosing an import policy.
Reject foreign source hashes, out-of-range or duplicate sidecar ordinals, unsafe types, invalid schemas and exceeded hard input boundaries without external access or partial publication.
Preserve strict W behavior, native outcome classes, owned raw/canonical provenance, complete coverage of rejected occurrences, linear grouped diagnostics and isolated Core/PYZ behavior.

oracle.requirement_contract: `specroad evidence import junit <FILE>` MUSS das dokumentierte JUnit-XML-Kernprofil aus Testsuites, Testsuite, Testcase, Failure, Error, Skipped, System-out und System-err ohne Testausführung einlesen können.
oracle.scope: 12.f.W/R/C reads bounded passive JUnit core XML. 12.g.W/R adds strict exact-attribute candidates and complete context-aware mapping analysis, explicitly source-bound external IDs and separate diagnostics. The strict W API remains compatible. This is not the global import CLI, original-attachment publication or verified external execution.

open_items: The global evidence import junit command, cross-format diagnostic integration, abort/skip import policy, original attachments, complete run/subject/configuration binding and atomic publication remain later plan work.
Synthetic parser/mapping observations do not authenticate an external run or prove project-wide verification, release readiness or approval.
